phase_a.identity_key_census_rule: Captain rule, 2026-08-01 addendum: the identity-key and live-case counts above are a certified FLOOR and a partition rule, not an expected observation. Ordinary intake keeps minting keys and keeps promoting exception cases to confirmed_live_job, so a3/a4 assert the invariants those numbers protect - every key lands in exactly one of live-job / exception-only / synthetic, no key or live case is destroyed (no negative growth from the floor), promotion only runs exception -> live, the synthetic set stays closed, and a confirmed_live_job case always has its job - and report growth above the floor instead of failing it. Pinning the exact counts is what made the certificate fail on healthy +3 live-job intake growth on 2026-08-01. Do not re-pin them; if a count must move DOWN, that is a real defect and the invariant is meant to catch it.

The expected count is the invariant, not the observation: if this check fails, adjudicate the offending card and add it to card_work_order_identity_exceptions under its own decision key, never raise the number.
